title: Flattening a finite type quasi-coherent module by an admissible blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], with finite presentation of module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is of finite presentation and flat over $U$ (at every $x\in X_U$, its stalk is flat over $\mathcal O_{U,f(x)}$). Then there is a $U$-admissible blowup $S'\to S$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] such that the strict transform $\mathcal F'$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform] is flat over $S'$ and is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_{X\times_S S'}$-module.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module (the module flattening theorem immediately preceding the scheme flattening lemma).

proof.text: First prove only flatness of the strict transform, for all data in the statement. Since $S$ and $X\to S$ are quasi-compact and locally finite presentation implies locally finite type, $X\to S$ is of finite type and $X$ is quasi-compact. The uniform fibre-dimension bound [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] bounds the dimensions of all fibre supports. Use strong induction on an integer $d\geq-1$ bounding $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$ for every $s$, with the empty support assigned dimension $-1$. For $d=-1$, every fibre module is zero; the residue-field criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] gives $\mathcal F=0$. The unit-ideal blowup is the identity and its strict transform is zero, hence flat.

source.place: Tag 0815, proof paragraph 1; induction base made explicit.

proof.text: Assume the flatness assertion for every smaller bound than $d\geq0$. By [lem-trf-etale-flattening-descent] it suffices to solve it on etale neighbourhoods covering $X$, with quasi-compact etale base neighbourhoods. Finite subcovers suffice since $X$ is quasi-compact. In particular take finite affine open charts of the base and then of the source. The bases can be made jointly surjective even when $X\to S$ is not surjective: adjoin diagrams with source $\varnothing$ and affine base charts, for which the unit-ideal blowup already solves flatness. At points outside the closed support of $\mathcal F$, use its zero restriction. Thus fix a point $x$ of a fibre support and affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $s=f(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0815, first paragraph; Tag 0814, finite etale covering hypotheses.

proof.text: Put $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)\leq d$. Apply [lem-trf-elementary-module-devissage]. It gives affine etale neighbourhoods $X',S'$, a finitely presented closed immersion $i:Z'\to X'$, a finite $\pi:Z'\to Y'$, and $\mathcal G$ with $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$, where $Y'\to S'$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ with geometrically integral fibres. Set $\mathcal N=\pi_*\mathcal G$. It is finite type and quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-f3-finite-pushforward-finite-type]. We will flatten $\mathcal N$ on this smooth family, then recover flatness of $g^*\mathcal F$. This is a local replacement around every point, including those where the local fibre-support dimension is smaller than $d$.

Check finite presentation over the preserved open before making this replacement. On affine charts over $S'$, $X'$ is finitely presented over $S'$; the same holds for $Z'$ because $i$ is finitely presented. Smoothness gives finite presentation of the affine $Y'$ over $S'$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra] makes the finite morphism $\pi$ finitely presented as well. Restrict $S\prime$ to an affine open of the preserved open when checking finite presentation over $U$. Since all the maps to $S\prime$ here are affine, the three source restrictions are affine. Write $B,C,D$ for the rings of $X\prime,Z\prime,Y\prime$ on these restrictions, with $C=B/J$. The module underlying $\mathcal G$ is finitely presented over $B$ because $i_*\mathcal G=g^*\mathcal F$ is so: tensor a finite presentation on $X_U$ with the affine chart ring of $X\prime$ to obtain a finite presentation of the pullback. It is finitely presented over $C$: for a presentation $B^a\to B^b\to M\to0$, the kernel of $C^b\to M$ is the image of the finitely generated kernel of $B^b\to M$. The finite finitely presented algebra $C/D$ is a finitely presented $D$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-presentation-module-presentation], and transitivity [lem-pc-module-finite-presentation-transitive] makes $\mathcal N_U$ finitely presented over $Y'_U$. Affine module presentations are identified with sheaf presentations by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine].

source.place: Tag 0815, second paragraph hypotheses; Algebra Tags 00F4, 0561, 0564.

proof.text: Check relative flatness under the paired etale neighbourhoods as well. On affine charts write $R\to A\to B$ for the original base, original source, and etale source neighbourhood, and write $R\to R'$ for the etale base neighbourhood. If $N$ is $R$-flat, then $B\otimes_A N$ is $R$-flat: for an injection $L\to L'$ of $R$-modules, tensor first with $N$, then with the flat $A$-algebra $B$, using $L\otimes_R(B\otimes_A N)=B\otimes_A(L\otimes_RN)$. Flatness of $B/A$ is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. The $R'$-action is the one provided by the diagram. Since $R'/R$ is etale, its diagonal is open and its differentials vanish [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism]; by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero] it is formally unramified, and it is finite type. Apply [lem-sc-unramified-flat-of-base-flat] to conclude $R'$-flatness. The affine relative-flatness criterion converts this back into stalk flatness. Thus $g^*\mathcal F$ really is relatively flat over $U\times_SS'$ before its affine pushforwards are taken.

source.place: Tag 0815, second paragraph, relative flatness hypotheses; flat.tex Tag 05B9 and its affine unramified generalization.

proof.text: Relative flatness is preserved and reflected by either affine pushforward here. Indeed on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, pushforward retains exactly the same underlying $R$-module. Apply [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion] on both affine schemes: flatness of this module over $R$ is equivalent to relative stalk flatness. Consequently $\mathcal G_U$ and $\mathcal N_U$ are flat over $U\times_SS'$. The same argument works after every base blowup. By [lem-trf-strict-transform-affine-pushforward], the strict transform of $i_*\mathcal G$ is $i_{b,*}\mathcal G^b$ and that of $\pi_*\mathcal G$ is $\pi_{b,*}\mathcal G^b$. Thus flattening $\mathcal N$ suffices to flatten $g^*\mathcal F$, with every comparison on the actual fibre products.

source.place: Tag 0815, second paragraph; Morphisms Tag 0FLM, affine module calculation; Divisors Tag 080G.

proof.text: We are reduced to affine $X\to S$ smooth of relative dimension $n\leq d$ with geometrically integral fibres, and a finite-type module $\mathcal F$ finitely presented and flat over $U$. Smoothness gives flatness and finite presentation. Apply [lem-trf-generic-free-blowup] to obtain a $U$-admissible blowup and a fibrewise nonempty open $V$ where the strict transform is finite locally free. Work on affine base charts after this blowup. The family remains smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] (2); its fibres remain geometrically integral of dimension $n$, by the meaning of geometric integrality and [lem-pc-dim-base-change]. The module remains finite type and retains its prescribed restriction over $U$ by [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus]. That calculus also identifies any subsequent strict transform with a single admissible blowup of the original local base.

source.place: Tag 0815, third paragraph, first two sentences; Tag 0811.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and the generic point $\xi$ of the integral fibre $X_s$. Since $V_s$ is nonempty it contains $\xi$. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathcal F=\widetilde N$. Choose finitely many elements of $N$ whose images are a basis of $N\otimes_A\kappa(\xi)$; fractions can be cleared by their invertible denominators in $\kappa(\xi)$. They define $\alpha:A^{\oplus r}\to N$. On a neighbourhood inside $V$, the module is finite free; a nonvanishing determinant minor therefore makes $\alpha$ an isomorphism on an open $W$ containing $\xi$. The image of $W$ in $S$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-finite-presentation-open]; replace $S$ by an affine neighbourhood of $s$ in that image. Now $W\to S$ is surjective, so $\alpha$ is an isomorphism at the generic point of every fibre. On $W$ the module is relatively flat, since the family is flat and the module is free there.

source.place: Tag 0815, third paragraph: choice of alpha, isomorphism open W and shrinking the base.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal H=\operatorname{coker}(\alpha)$. Apply [lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness] to $R\to A$ and $N$. Its generic-basis and generic-flatness hypotheses hold by the preceding step. Hence $0\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal H\to0$ remains exact after every base change, and $\mathcal H$ has the same relative flat locus as $\mathcal F$. In particular $\mathcal H_U$ is flat. It is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-cokernel], since $\mathcal O_{X_U}^{\oplus r}$ is finite type and $\mathcal F_U$ is finitely presented. The cokernel is finite type and quasi-coherent, as is seen directly by taking the cokernel of the corresponding modules on affine charts.

source.place: Tag 0815, third paragraph: universal injectivity and definition of H.

proof.text: The induction bound strictly decreases. For each $s$, $\mathcal H_s$ vanishes on the nonempty open $W_s$ of the integral $n$-dimensional fibre $X_s$. Its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type], so it is a proper closed subset. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets in this support extends by appending $X_s$, and therefore has length at most $n-1$. Thus $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal H_s)\leq n-1<d$ (or $\leq d-1$ when $n=d$). For $n=0$ the proper closed subset is empty. Apply the induction hypothesis to $\mathcal H$ with bound $n-1$, including its base case if $n=0$: all the finite-type, finite-presentation-over-$U$, and relative-flatness-over-$U$ hypotheses were checked above. It yields an admissible blowup on which $\mathcal H^b$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 0815, third paragraph, induction application; dimension decrease made explicit.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-strict-transform-universal-exact] the strict transforms fit into $0\to(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r})^b\to\mathcal F^b\to\mathcal H^b\to0$. Because $X\to S$ is flat, [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] identifies the first term with $\mathcal O_{X\times_SS^b}^{\oplus r}$. On $W\times_SS^b$ the strict transform of $\mathcal F$ is its finite free pullback, by the same calculus applied to the restriction. This open is fibrewise nonempty: nonempty fibres remain nonempty after a field extension, since tensoring a nonzero vector space with a field extension is faithful. Thus the transformed map is again a basis at every fibre generic point and $\mathcal F^b$ is flat there. Apply [lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness] on each affine chart of $S^b$: its cokernel is precisely $\mathcal H^b$ by the displayed exact sequence, and is flat by construction. The flatness equivalence gives flatness of $\mathcal F^b$ everywhere. This solves the smooth local problem.

source.place: Tag 0815, third paragraph: displayed exact sequence and transfer of flatness from H to F.

proof.text: Combine the preliminary blowup with the induction blowup by [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus], retaining its specified centre with zero set the union of the two centre supports. Apply [lem-trf-etale-flattening-descent] first to the affine base neighbourhoods of the smooth family, then to the original elementary devissage neighbourhoods. Step 6 transfers the solved flatness back across $\pi$ and $i$. Quasi-compactness extracts finite source covers at each gluing. Include the empty-source base charts described in step 2 if needed. Thus the induction is complete and a single $U$-admissible blowup makes the original module strict transform flat.

source.place: Tag 0815, paragraphs 1--3; Tag 0814; successive blowups as in Tag 080Y.

proof.text: It remains to establish finite presentation of that strict transform. On the flattened (qcqs) base, [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] gives a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal whose zero set is the complement of the preserved quasi-compact open $U$; apply [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier] to it. It gives a further admissible blowup on which $U$ is scheme-theoretically dense. Since the module is already relatively flat, [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] says its new strict transform is its pullback, hence still flat and finite type. Its restriction over $U$ is still the original finitely presented module. The ambient morphism is still locally of finite presentation by affine base change [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. The base is qcqs, so its quasi-compact open $U$ is retrocompact: its intersection with each quasi-compact open is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness. Apply [lem-trf-flat-finite-type-dense-presentation] to conclude finite presentation on the entire ambient fibre product. Finally compose the two base blowups using the calculus, including the module strict-transform identification. The resulting blowup has both conclusions of the item.
